lines: Nightpaw! I can hear you!
It's warm up here, and there's water everywhere, like a bath.
The moth says I'll be the brightest thing in the whole Underneath.
...Why does everyone look so sad?
Somewhere above, a music box is playing a waltz.
Nobody is winding it.
NIGHTPAW ↑
and underneath, smaller: (its WET)
Mira's chalk. The last letter is smudged, as if she wiped her hand on her nightie.
A CAT! In MY bath! Oh, this is the best day. Every day is the best day, but this one especially.
I'm Dunk. I float. Watch.
Still floating! Amazing.
You're looking for the girl with the ribbon! She waved at me. Nobody's waved at me in forty years.
She lost the ribbon in the cot. She was going to go back for it, but the moth said no time, no time.
They went up. Past the Queen. Everyone who goes up goes past the Queen.
Oh! And you can't climb that shaft. Cats can't climb walls. Everybody knows that.
Unless they've got the mittens. The velvet ones, in the Toy Chest, through there. With the pins in.
Mind the boxes. They pop.
Still floating!
The Toy Chest is through the door past the candles. Mittens. Velvet. Pins. Pop.
You found the mittens! Now you can climb the shaft! You're a climbing cat now. A cat that climbs.
Up there is the Tidewheel. The water goes up and down, up and down. Like me, but sideways.
Wait for it to go up.
The music stopped. I didn't know it could stop.
It's very quiet. I think I like it. I think I'm sad. Can you be both?
Still floating, though.
Good evening. I flew up the draught. It was very undignified.
Somebody has to light the candles, and nobody up here remembers how.
I know this room. We all do, all of Mothmother's moths.
This was her nursery. Before she was Mothmother, she was a nightlight, shaped like a moth, on that shelf there.
A child loved her very much. Then the child grew up, and the nightlight was lost.
She never stopped wanting to be somebody's light.
I'm telling you so you understand her. Not so you forgive her. I haven't decided about that myself.
Rest by the candle whenever you like. It's the least I can do. Well. It's the most I can do. It's about all I can do.

steps.title: Mira's Ribbon
steps.text: Red, to match the scarf. It still smells like her shampoo.

lines: ...lose a ribbon off a tree...
I dropped it, Nightpaw. The moth wouldn't let me go back.
If you find it, keep it for me. You can wear it. You'd look very handsome.
The inside of the chest is very deep, and the walls are very smooth.
At the bottom, something soft is glowing.
A pair of velvet mittens, very small, with the pins still in them.
Somebody was making them for a doll. Or a cat.

steps.title: Velvet Claws
steps.text: Soft on the outside. Not on the inside.
steps.hint: Hold toward a wall to cling to it. Jump to leap off. Clinging refreshes your double jump and dash.

steps.text: Climb out: jump between the walls.
The water rises and falls with the music. Ride it up.

steps.title: The Third Life — The Fireworks Night
lines: Bang. Bang. The sky coming apart in colours.
You ran and ran and went up the only place that was dark and small: the chimney.
It was very warm in there, and it smelled of old toast.
Then it was very warm, and then it was very quiet.
In the morning Mira drew you a picture with forty-one stars on it, so you would never be scared of the sky again.

steps.title: A Life Remembered
steps.text: One of your lost lives has come home.
Too far to jump. Jump, jump again, then dash.
Every doll on every shelf is looking at you.

lines: Hush now, hush, and hold on tight...
There. Now you're all tucked in. You look scared. You don't have to be scared.
I'll come back and wind you all up. I promise. Pinky promise.

steps.text: One of the dolls, very slowly, closes its eyes.

lines: SHE SINGS TO THEM
Not Mira's writing. Much older. The chalk is almost gone.

steps.title: Mira's Drawing
steps.text: A black cat wearing a crown, and a red scarf, and a very serious expression. Underneath: KING NIGHTPAW.

lines: Not yet, little light.
Not yet.
Oh. Someone came.
Sixty years I have danced in this box. Sixty years, and nobody came back to wind me.
The little girl came. She hummed along. She said she would come back.
They all say that.
Well. You are here now, little cat. So you shall watch me dance.
You shall watch me dance forever.
Slower... the music is going slower...
The little girl. She hummed. She didn't know the tune, so she hummed her own.
Lose a penny, lose a key...
She went up the chain, with the moth. To the market, and the lamp beyond it.
Tell her... tell her the Queen said thank you. For the humming.
I think I can stop now.

steps.text: Somewhere far below, a plug is pulled. The whole nursery begins, very slowly, to drain.

lines: You again! The cat with no pockets!
I'm packing. You heard that music stop? That's the Nursery going quiet. Quiet's bad for business.
Market's up through the plughole. Mousewick. Loudest place in the whole Underneath.
Is that a ribbon? Red? Real silk? I'll give you three buttons for it.
No? Four. No? Fine. Keep your sentimental ribbon.
Your girl came through here an hour ago, holding a moth's hand. Or a moth's leg. Whatever moths have.
Come up to the market. I'll have my shop open. There will be hats.
Up through the plughole. Mind the drop. Mind the mice. Mind your manners.
Through the plughole, a roar of voices, bells, wheels, and a thousand small feet.
It smells of cheese and brass polish.
Nightpaw, there's a whole town of mice! They're selling buttons!
The moth says we can't stop. She's in a hurry. She keeps looking at me like I'm a candle.
...Nightpaw? Hurry up.
